name: folio

scripts.pages:build: VITE_BASE=/folio/ npm run build && node tools/stamp-sw.mjs dist
scripts.author: node --experimental-strip-types tools/authoring/cli.ts
scripts.coverage:all: mkdir -p .coverage && npm run coverage:unit >.coverage/unit.log 2>&1 && npm run e2e >.coverage/e2e.log 2>&1 && node tools/coverage-report.mjs --per-file

comment:coverage-combined: Combined coverage measured 97.87-97.92% over six runs (2026-10-31): five on the dev box and one in CI. It then rose to 98.00-98.04% once the e2e collected uncaught errors properly and three vacuous assertions were replaced with real ones. Floor is 97.5, set from the LOWER measurement set and left there: 0.37pp of headroom below the first minimum and 0.5pp below the second. The margin is deliberate and larger than the 0.06pp the old floor used: CON-COV-002 forbids lowering a floor, so an over-tight one has to be walked back and an over-loose one merely ratchets again. What still drifts is src/shader.ts by about three lines a run (0.03pp) in its uniform-setup path. The thing that USED to drift — destroy() and the webglcontextlost handler, 13 lines, once in three runs — is deterministic now: the e2e fires WEBGL_lose_context.loseContext() rather than hoping a page detaches the canvas before closing. The recorded cause for that swing (headless Chrome refusing a WebGL context) was wrong; a probe granted one 9 times out of 9. Never raise this on a single run.
comment:coverage-logs: coverage:all sends the unit and e2e output to .coverage/*.log rather than /dev/null. They used to go nowhere, so when the e2e failed inside a coverage run the chain stopped with no way to see WHICH check failed — the gate said only "1 check(s) failed". Read .coverage/e2e.log when coverage:gate exits non-zero without printing a coverage figure.
comment:coverage-floor: coverage:gate hardcodes the floor rather than relying on `npm run X -- --min N`. The passthrough is npm-version dependent: it applied in CI and silently did NOT apply locally, which would have left the gate unable to fail after an npm upgrade. Hardcode, like test:gate.
comment:coverage: test:gate floors are a RATCHET — raise them in the PR that earns the improvement, never lower them to make a build green (CON-COV-002). These are the UNIT-only floors; the combined floor lives in coverage:gate and is documented above. Baseline 38.91/74.52/39.41 set 2026-09-20 when import-all first forced the whole of src/ into the denominator (the previously reported 87.65% measured only five files). Phase 1 raised it to 86.05/71.67/75.42 — branches fell because newly-covered files brought their unexercised branches into the denominator, which is the honest direction. This field used to say "Destination is 95" and "remaining climb to 95 needs browser-side coverage (shader/engine/tilt)": both were left standing after the combined floor passed 95 and reached 97.5, so the record contradicted the gate it describes — the same stale-note failure task 14c was closed for.
comment:author: The AI authoring pipeline (npm run author) needs @anthropic-ai/sdk. Install it on demand — `npm i -D @anthropic-ai/sdk` — it is not part of the app build.
